reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that DNN potentials were trained via active learning on AIMD data for high-entropy carbonitrides and used to simulate melting, but it does not provide any comparison with EAM potentials, nor does it quantify phase-space overlap or thermodynamic-integration path mismatch. Thus, the key premises about superiority over EAM and reduction in mismatch are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: DNN potentials trained via active learning on AIMD data can represent liquid configurations of high-entropy alloys more accurately than EAM potentials.
Improved representation of the ab initio energy landscape by DNN potentials enhances reference–target phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
The approach is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy carbonitrides near their high melting temperatures (~3500 K).
